setting: A deep-space research station near a neutron star forty light-years away. Fictional story.

characters.narrator: Calm, wondrous narrator who sets the scene and reveals key facts.
characters.female: Mara, the station's navigator. The signal says her name. She speaks in first person when she is the one talking.
characters.male_brit: Commander Hale, the calm leader and skeptic. He wants safety above all.
characters.young: Jin, the young engineer who found the signal. Brave and curious.
characters.old: Dr. Ruth, the oldest scientist. She knows the station's history and the star's past.
characters.gruff: Voss, security chief. Blunt and suspicious. Also used for 'The Eighth', the unseen presence.

rules: Each episode is 30-40 seconds with 6-12 scenes and 2-4 speakers in the same room.
Characters talk to each other, not just to the viewer.
Open with a short recap line, then advance the story.
End on a cliffhanger, except the final episode, which resolves the story.
Every episode ends with a choice for viewers, for example 'Comment A or B'.
beats: The signal says Mara's name for the first time.
The source is a neutron star forty light-years away, and a countdown begins.
Commander Hale orders silence, and the lights start flickering.
An eighth voice speaks inside the room, but the crew counts only seven.
Dr. Ruth recognizes the pulse pattern from old station records.
Jin finds a hidden log dated sixty years ago.
The log is written in Mara's handwriting.
Voss seals the station, and the main door will not open.
The countdown reaches one thousand, then pauses.
The Eighth shows each crew member a glimpse of their own future.
The crew argues, and Hale wants to abort the mission.
Mara walks to the signal console in her sleep.
Jin discovers the signal is a map of the station itself.
A second station appears on the screen, identical to theirs.
Ruth reveals that the first crew vanished at the same star.
Voss opens a sealed room with eight beds in it.
The eighth bed has Mara's name tag on it.
Mara's memories have gaps, and she starts counting again.
Hale sends a message to Earth, and a reply arrives in his own voice.
The power dies, and emergency lights show a figure in the corridor.
The Eighth offers a deal: one person can leave the station alive.
The crew votes, and the vote is a tie.
Jin sacrifices his oxygen to open a vent and let Mara through.
The station splits in two, and both halves think they are the original.
Ruth decodes the signal and finds it is an invitation.
Mara realizes the Eighth is her, from another timeline.
Hale chooses to go with the Eighth to save the rest of the crew.
The crew must decide whether to destroy the star.
The countdown stops, and the galaxy falls silent.
Finale: the crew hears eight voices from far away, saying they are still counting.
